blocks.content: NITI Aayog is an advisory think tank without financial powers to allocate funds, relying entirely on the Ministry of Finance for budgetary allocations.

rows: Allocated funds to ministries and state governments
No financial allocation powers; purely advisory
Formulated Five-Year Plans and allocated budgetary grants
Generates long-term policy vision, strategy, and action agendas

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: NITI Aayog serves purely as an advisory think tank and lacks the financial power to allocate funds to states or central ministries.
The authority to disburse plan expenditure and central allocations to states was entirely transferred to the Ministry of Finance.
Like its predecessor, NITI Aayog is an extra-constitutional, non-statutory body established via an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet.
Critics highlight that without financial leverage, NITI Aayog struggles to enforce national development priorities across states.
The body lacks executive implementation machinery, depending entirely on central ministries and state governments to execute its vision documents.
NITI Aayog does NOT possess fund allocation powers; this power resides with the Ministry of Finance.
NITI Aayog is neither a statutory body nor a constitutional body—it was created by an executive resolution.
Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog cannot grant plan expenditure to state governments.
